correctness.rationale: For fixed G,p,c the scalar variable x=hcλ/2 on a positive eigenvalue tends to infinity and the binomial expansion gives r_p(x)=p/x+O(x^-2), independently of any finite test. Squaring, multiplying by hλ and summing the finitely many spectral projectors yields the exact 4p²/(c²h) coefficient of L⁺ with matrix-norm O(h^-2), with the constant space unaffected. A strictly positive off-diagonal of L⁺ therefore makes that same entry negative at sufficiently large h. The scalar subtraction is (2/c)x r_p(x)^2 where x r_p(x)^2 is continuous, nonnegative, zero at zero and tends to zero at infinity; c≥4C_p proves the [1/2,1] spectrum simultaneously and for all h≥0. Unit-path resistances are distances |i−j|. Double-centering −HDH/2 using sums n(n−1)/2, 1+(n−2)(n−1)/2 and n(n²−1)/3 gives (n−1)(2n−7)/(6n) at 12, strictly positive for n≥4. Thus every fixed finite order has the path obstruction, rather than just a check for a finite list of orders.
